name: What is bathroom waterproofing and why is it necessary behind tile?

mainEntity.name: What is bathroom waterproofing and why is it necessary behind tile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom waterproofing involves applying a continuous barrier beneath tile, stone, and wall surfaces to stop water from reaching framing and drywall. During a shower or bathroom remodel, a contractor installs water-resistant backing boards, pre-formed pans, or liquid and sheet membranes across the shower pan, walls, and tub surrounds before setting any finish tile. Seams, screw penetrations, and plumbing cutouts must be treated with waterproof banding or sealant. Without a complete waterproof layer behind the tile, water and moisture inevitably seep through porous grout lines, causing hidden wood rot, structural weakening, and mold growth inside wall cavities over time.
acceptedAnswer.description: Bathroom waterproofing creates an impermeable barrier behind tile and backer boards to stop water and steam from rotting wood framing or growing mold inside wall cavities.
